title: How Was the Bible Transmitted?
subtitle: From spoken word to Greek manuscripts to modern translations — the journey of the Christian scriptures, told honestly
summary: The Bible reached the present through many authors, collections, translations, and hand-copied manuscripts. This history preserves valuable ancient testimony but also produced textual variants and debated passages. Islam distinguishes the original revelations given to Moses and Jesus from the later textual collections and presents the Quran as the preserved final criterion over them.

seo.metaTitle: How Was the Bible Transmitted? An Honest History
seo.metaDescription: The Bible preserves genuine ancient testimony, but it reached readers through many authors, manuscripts, languages, and later decisions about the canon.

sections.title: The Evidence in Brief
sections.body: The Bible preserves genuine ancient testimony, but it reached readers through many authors, manuscripts, languages, and later decisions about the canon. Textual criticism can recover much of its wording with confidence while also identifying passages whose earliest form is uncertain. Islam honors the revelations given to Moses and Jesus, yet presents the Quran as the final criterion by which earlier claims are judged.

sections.title: From Early Writings to Modern Bibles
sections.body:
The Hebrew Bible and New Testament are libraries of writings produced and copied over long periods. No original manuscript survives. Scholars compare thousands of later manuscripts, ancient translations, and quotations to estimate the earliest recoverable wording. This work succeeds for most of the text while leaving some passages uncertain.

Most differences are spelling, word order, or other small copying changes. A smaller group is more significant: the longer ending of Mark, the story of the woman accused of adultery, and the Trinitarian wording in 1 John 5:7 are familiar examples identified in modern translations. Canon is a separate question: Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant churches do not include exactly the same Old Testament books.

sections.title: The Quran's View of Earlier Scripture
sections.body: The Quran affirms that God revealed the Torah and Gospel, criticizes concealment and distortion by some people, and describes the Quran as confirming earlier scripture and acting as a criterion over it (Quran 5:48). Islam therefore avoids two extremes: it does not say every biblical sentence is false, and it does not treat every surviving form as identical to pristine revelation. Agreement with the Quran is affirmed; conflict is judged by the final revelation.

sections.title: How the Biblical Texts Reached the Present
sections.body: The biblical books were composed and collected over centuries. Luke 1:1–4 openly explains that many accounts already existed and that its author investigated the received reports before writing an ordered narrative. The manuscripts were then copied by hand, producing spelling differences, omissions, additions, and larger disputed passages. Textual criticism compares witnesses to reconstruct the earliest recoverable wording. This work is valuable and often successful, but an earliest recoverable reading is still a scholarly reconstruction from surviving copies rather than an original manuscript preserved intact.

sections.title: Two Transmission Stories, Side by Side
sections.body:
Set the two transmission stories side by side — each as its own scholarship tells it — and structural differences emerge.

Language: the Quran is preserved and recited in its original Arabic, while the words of Jesus were spoken in Aramaic but preserved in Greek — with few exceptions, not available in his own tongue.

Timescale: Muslim tradition and the early manuscript record describe a complete text standardized within a generation of the Prophet Muhammad's death, while the New Testament canon took shape over centuries.

Mechanism: the Quran's transmission ran on two parallel tracks — mass memorization alongside written copies — each checking the other; the Bible's ran on hand copying alone, which is why variants accumulated and textual criticism became necessary.

Self-description: Luke's prologue describes research and compilation of handed-down reports; the Quran presents itself throughout as the direct speech of God to one messenger.

sections.title: Common Misconceptions
sections.body:
A few misunderstandings cloud this topic on both sides.

"Muslims believe the Bible is worthless." Not so. The Quran calls the original Torah and Gospel guidance and light and calls Christians the People of the Gospel. The Islamic claim concerns transmission, not a denial that God spoke through Jesus.

"Textual variants mean nobody knows what the Bible says." Also not so. Mainstream textual critics hold that the vast majority of variants are minor and the general shape of the text is well established. The serious questions concern specific passages and wording — significant, but not a free-for-all.

"The books of the Bible were chosen at the Council of Nicaea." This story circulates in novels and internet memes, but historians of Christianity describe canon formation as a gradual process reflected in usage, debate, and later lists and councils. Repeating the Nicaea legend weakens any argument built on it.

sections.title: Why the Quranic Criterion Matters
sections.body:
The Quran says:

وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ

'We have revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming what preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it' (Quran 5:48). The transmission history explains why such a criterion is needed. Islam preserves respect for God's earlier messengers while locating final textual authority in the Quran.

sections.title: The Central Takeaway
sections.body: The Bible remains historically and religiously important, but its long, decentralized transmission requires reconstruction and interpretation. The Quran offers a different preservation history and claims to restore the unambiguous call of the prophets: worship God alone.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Did Jesus write any part of the Bible?
A: No. Mainstream Christian scholarship agrees that Jesus left no writings. The Gospels were written about him, in Greek, in the decades after his ministry — a process Luke describes in his prologue.

Q: Do Muslims believe the Bible is completely corrupted?
A: No. The Quran affirms the original Torah and Gospel as guidance and light, and classical scholars differed over whether the distortion it warns of affected mainly the text or its interpretation. Today's Bible is seen as containing truth alongside material shaped by long human transmission.

Q: What language did Jesus speak, and why does it matter?
A: Historians broadly agree Jesus taught in Aramaic, while the New Testament was composed in Greek. With few exceptions, his words reach us in translation — a fact acknowledged in standard Christian scholarship.

Q: Who decided which books belong in the Bible?
A: No single meeting decided it. Books circulated and were debated for generations; the earliest surviving exact list of today's twenty-seven New Testament books comes from Athanasius in the later fourth century, and Christian communions still differ over the Old Testament canon.

Q: Is textual criticism an attack on Christianity?
A: No. It is a discipline built largely by Christian scholars seeking the earliest recoverable wording of the Bible. The manuscript footnotes in modern Christian Bibles are the fruit of that work.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:

- **The Text of the New Testament: Its Transmission, Corruption, and Restoration** — Bruce M. Metzger and Bart D. Ehrman. The standard scholarly introduction to New Testament textual criticism.
- **The Canon of the New Testament: Its Origin, Development, and Significance** — Bruce M. Metzger. A detailed history of how the twenty-seven-book New Testament canon took shape.
- **The Canon of Scripture** — F. F. Bruce. An evangelical Christian scholar's account of canon formation for both Testaments.
- **Misquoting Jesus: The Story Behind Who Changed the Bible and Why** — Bart D. Ehrman. A popular-level introduction to manuscripts and variants; its conclusions are debated among scholars.
- **The History of the Qur'anic Text from Revelation to Compilation: A Comparative Study with the Old and New Testaments** — Muhammad Mustafa al-Azami. A Muslim scholar's comparative study of Quranic and biblical transmission.

quranVerses.arabic: وَقَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِعِيسَى ٱبْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًۭى وَنُورٌۭ وَمُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَهُدًۭى وَمَوْعِظَةًۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ ٱلْإِنجِيلِ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ ۚ وَمَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًۭا ۖ فَوَيْلٌۭ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌۭ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ
quranVerses.translation: So woe to those who write the "scripture" with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," in order to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ ۚ لِكُلٍّۢ جَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ شِرْعَةًۭ وَمِنْهَاجًۭا ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِى مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۖ فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ ۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًۭا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us, even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us, it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus; that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.
There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.
Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
For there are three who testify:
